themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase (z-score: 3.4)—suggesting either new unlicensed dispensaries opening in Midtown or escalating neighbor complaints about existing legal retailers.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.4, severity: high)
Timing coincides with possible new retail licenses or enforcement actions
reporting_angles: Map where these complaints originated; are they clustered around specific addresses or blocks?
Interview SLA and OCME about licensing activity in CD 105 over the past month

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violations of park rules jumped to 17 complaints 2 WEEKS AGO versus 2.6 weekly average—a 548% increase (z-score: 3.49)—pointing to emerging disorder, encampments, or unauthorized activities in Midtown parks, aligning with long-standing CB budget requests for enhanced park safety.
evidence: 17 park rules violation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 3.49, severity: high)
Community Board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety and security staff funding (ongoing budget priority)
reporting_angles: Identify which parks in Midtown (Central Park, Madison Square Park, etc.) are generating complaints; what specific violations are being reported?
Interview Parks Enforcement Patrol about staffing levels and incident response times

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints reached 25 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 12.1 weekly average—a 106% spike (z-score: 5.84, highest severity)—indicating possible unlicensed street food operations or enforcement crackdowns in Midtown's high-traffic commercial areas.
evidence: 25 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 12.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.84, severity: high)
Highest z-score among current spikes, indicating strongest statistical deviation
reporting_angles: Are complaints about unlicensed vendors, health code violations, or obstruction of sidewalk space? Map complaint hotspots.
Interview DOHMH Vending Unit about enforcement activity; check for recent summonses or confiscations

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping in Public Spaces
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints jumped to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 1.6 weekly average—a 269% spike (z-score: 3.32)—suggesting emerging enforcement or a genuine uptick in public smoking/vaping violations, particularly relevant in dense Midtown commercial areas.
evidence: 6 smoking/vaping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.32, severity: high)
Pattern may reflect seasonal outdoor activity increase or new enforcement focus
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaints against DOHMH tobacco enforcement records
Interview Parks Enforcement or NYPD about smoking/vaping violation enforcement strategy

themes_detail.label: Building Condition Complaints (Flooring/Stairs)
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stair complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.6 weekly average—a 540% increase (z-score: 4.85)—possibly signaling a localized structural issue, deferred maintenance, or hazardous conditions in one or more Midtown buildings amid high DOB permit activity (3,839 filings in 90 days).
evidence: 4 flooring/stair complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85, severity: high)
3,839 DOB alteration/new building permits filed in 90 days; 32 full demolitions suggest heavy construction activity
reporting_angles: Map complaints to specific addresses; identify if they cluster around active construction sites or older buildings
Cross-reference with DOB violation records and 311 complaint addresses to see if single building or multiple sites are involved
